blocks.prompt: 11 In how many ways can a hockey team of 11 players be selected out of 15 players? how many of them will include a particular player?
blocks.explanation:
Two questions in one: all teams, then teams that contain one particular player.
A team is a selection (order does not matter).
Plan: \({}^{15}C_{11}\); then fix the particular player and choose 10 out of the other 14: \({}^{14}C_{10}\).
steps:
Given: 15 players; team of 11.
To find: (1) all possible teams; (2) teams that include a particular player.
Method: combinations; use \({}^{n}C_{r} = {}^{n}C_{n-r}\) to shorten the work.

Part 1: all teams
\[{}^{15}C_{11} = {}^{15}C_{4}\]
\[= \dfrac{15 \cdot 14 \cdot 13 \cdot 12}{4 \cdot 3 \cdot 2 \cdot 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{32760}{24} = 1365\]
Why: Choosing 11 to play is the same as choosing the 4 who sit out.

Part 2: the particular player is in
\[\text{places left} = 10,\ \text{players left} = 14\]
\[{}^{14}C_{10} = {}^{14}C_{4}\]
\[= \dfrac{14 \cdot 13 \cdot 12 \cdot 11}{24}\]
\[= \dfrac{24024}{24} = 1001\]
Why: He is already in the team, so we fill 10 places from the other 14.

Check
\[\text{without him} = {}^{14}C_{11} = {}^{14}C_{3} = 364\]
\[1001 + 364 = 1365 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Every team either includes him or does not.
blocks.final_answer: 1365 teams in all; 1001 of them include the particular player
